author: Max Büsken
publication: Calibrating the cosmic-ray energy scale of the Pierre Auger Observatory using radio detection of extensive air showers in AERA
facts: Five new remote CS110 stations installed August/November2022 and revisited November2023; all five sensor faces confirmed2m above ground.
Galvanized CM106BE tripods without optional extension, lightning rod or guy wires. Ground rod driven at least0.5m into soil, connected to sensor bracket.
Tripod-mounted WiMo29dBi grid dish below the sensor faces the opposite direction. CLF station uses buried fiber and has no such radio link.
Solar power uses100W36V monocrystalline panel and aluminum mount with lower panel edge about0.1m above soil. A closed0.8x0.6x0.410m ZARGES K470 electronics box rests on the mount.
guanaCO feet use earth nails and small cairns; the other new stations use bolted concrete supports.
New field-station fences are15x15m; guanaCO uses an existing BATATA fence. Fence boundaries/centroid offsets/rotations are not supplied and are excluded from the independent instrument assembly.
estimates: All mast diameters, leg spread, exact body dimensions/orientation, dish size, solar dimensions/tilt/offsets, color and minor fittings are original visualization estimates.
Exact ground-contact levels and component positions are not surveyed. Coordinates are rounded published station points; allow10m horizontal uncertainty.

Instrument assemblies are independent whole equipment bodies, not proxies for AERA or the entire observatory. Older CRS and AERAWS have different installations and are not modeled from this prototype.
